title: Cost Optimization and Caching Strategies
summary: This day covers essential concepts for building AI engineering skills.
content:
# Cost Optimization and Caching Strategies ##### ₹18.4 lakh a month, and 71% of it was one mistake A B2B SaaS company in Pune had a GenAI feature suite costing ₹18.4 lakh a month. Finance asked for a 40% reduction. The engineering team assumed this meant degrading quality. They started by instrumenting cost per feature, per request type, and per user — two days of work. The breakdown was not what anyone predicted: | Cost driver | Share | Root cause | |---|---|---| | Document summariser using GPT-4o | 44% | Never evaluated a smaller model | | Duplicate requests | 18% | No cache; UI had no "recent" list | | System prompt re-sent uncached | 9% | 2,800 tokens × every request | | Retrieving 15 chunks when 5 sufficed | 12% | Never measured the trade-off | | Genuinely necessary GPT-4o usage | 17% | — | **71% of the bill was addressable without touching quality.** Model routing, caching, prompt caching, and reducing `top_k` brought it to ₹4.9 lakh — a 73% reduction — and evaluation scores went *up* slightly, because fewer chunks meant less context dilution. **Cost optimisation in GenAI is almost always about waste, not about accepting worse output.** Day 42 of the beginner track introduced caching; today is the systematic version — measure first, then apply the levers in order of return. ##### Instrument before optimising You cannot reduce what you cannot attribute. This is the Pune team's two days. ```python from dataclasses import dataclass, field from collections import defaultdict from typing import Optional import time @dataclass class CostRecord: request_id: str feature: str user_id: str model: str tokens_in: int tokens_out: int cached_tokens: int = 0 cost_inr: float = 0.0 latency_ms: float = 0.0 cache_status: str = "miss" # "exact" | "semantic" | "prompt" | "miss" timestamp: float = field(default_factory=time.time) PRICING_INR_PER_1K = { "gpt-4o": {"in": 0.21, "out": 0.84, "cached_in": 0.105}, "gpt-4o-mini": {"in": 0.0125, "out": 0.050, "cached_in": 0.00625}, "claude-3-5-sonnet": {"in": 0.25, "out": 1.25, "cached_in": 0.025}, "claude-3-5-haiku": {"in": 0.067, "out": 0.33, "cached_in": 0.0067}, "llama-3-8b-selfhost": {"in": 0.002, "out": 0.002, "cached_in": 0.0}, "llama-3-70b-selfhost":{"in": 0.012, "out": 0.012, "cached_in": 0.0}, } def compute_cost(model: str, tokens_in: int, tokens_out: int, cached_tokens: int = 0) -> float: p = PRICING_INR_PER_1K.get(model) if not p: return 0.0 uncached_in = max(tokens_in - cached_tokens, 0) return (uncached_in / 1000 * p["in"] + cached_tokens / 1000 * p["cached_in"] + tokens_out / 1000 * p["out"]) class CostAnalyzer: """Attribute spend across every dimension that could be a lever.""" def __init__(self, records: list[CostRecord]): self.records = records def by_dimension(self, dim: str, top_n=10) -> list[dict]: buckets = defaultdict(lambda: {"cost": 0.0, "requests": 0, "tokens_in": 0, "tokens_out": 0}) for r in self.records: key = getattr(r, dim) b = buckets[key] b["cost"] += r.cost_inr b["requests"] += 1 b["tokens_in"] += r.tokens_in b["tokens_out"] += r.tokens_out total = sum(b["cost"] for b in buckets.values()) or 1.0 rows = [{dim: k, "cost_inr": round(v["cost"], 2), "pct_of_total": round(100 * v["cost"] / total, 1), "requests": v["requests"], "inr_per_request": round(v["cost"] / v["requests"], 4), "avg_tokens_in": v["tokens_in"] // v["requests"], "avg_tokens_out": v["tokens_out"] // v["requests"]} for k, v in buckets.items()] return sorted(rows, key=lambda x: -x["cost_inr"])[:top_n] def waste_analysis(self, embedder=None) -> dict: """Quantify the addressable waste before choosing a lever.""" import numpy as np total = sum(r.cost_inr for r in self.records) or 1.0 # 1. Exact duplicates seen, dup_cost = {}, 0.0 for r in self.records: key = (r.feature, r.model, r.tokens_in) if key in seen: dup_cost += r.cost_inr seen[key] = True # 2. Output-token dominance — usually a max_tokens problem out_heavy = [r for r in self.records if r.tokens_out > 800] # 3. Large-model usage on short prompts overkill = [r for r in self.records if r.model in ("gpt-4o", "claude-3-5-sonnet") and r.tokens_in < 500 and r.tokens_out < 200] # 4. Prompt caching left on the table uncached_large = [r for r in self.records if r.tokens_in > 1500 and r.cached_tokens == 0] return { "total_inr": round(total, 2), "duplicate_waste_pct": round(100 * dup_cost / total, 1), "output_heavy_pct": round( 100 * sum(r.cost_inr for r in out_heavy) / total, 1), "model_overkill_pct": round( 100 * sum(r.cost_inr for r in overkill) / total, 1), "uncached_prefix_pct": round( 100 * sum(r.cost_inr for r in uncached_large) / total, 1), } ``` **Tag every call with feature, user, and model** — Day 35's point, applied to cost. Without those tags the bill is one number nobody can act on. **Run `waste_analysis` first.** It tells you which lever to pull, and the answer is frequently not the one you expected. ##### The optimisation levers, ranked ```mermaid flowchart TD A["Instrument and attribute"] --> B{"Largest waste category?"} B -->|"Model overkill"| C["1. Model routing / cascade
50-80% saving"] B -->|"Duplicates"| D["2. Exact + semantic cache
20-60% saving"] B -->|"Uncached prefix"| E["3. Prompt caching
30-90% on input"] B -->|"Too much context"| F["4. Reduce top_k, compress
20-40% saving"] B -->|"Long outputs"| G["5. max_tokens, prompt for brevity
10-30% saving"] C --> H["6. Batch API for async work
50% saving"] D --> H E --> H F --> H G --> H H --> I["7. Self-host at volume
evaluate break-even"] ``` | Lever | Typical saving | Effort | Quality risk | |---|---|---|---| | **Model routing** | **50–80%** | Moderate | Low with verification | | **Exact caching** | 15–40% | Low | **None** | | **Prompt caching** | 30–90% of input cost | **Trivial** | **None** | | Semantic caching | 10–30% | Moderate | **Real — needs care** | | Reduce retrieved chunks | 20–40% | Low | Often *improves* quality | | Cap `max_tokens` | 10–30% | Trivial | Low | | Batch API | 50% on eligible work | Low | None (latency only) | | Self-hosting | 60–90% at volume | High | Low | **Prompt caching is the highest return per unit of effort** and the one most often skipped. It is usually a single argument. ##### Prompt caching Day 32 covered the mechanism. Here is the economics and the structural requirement. ```python from anthropic import Anthropic client = Anthropic() response = client.messages.create( model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022", max_tokens=1024, system=[ {"type": "text", "text": LONG_SYSTEM_PROMPT + "\n\n" + FEW_SHOT_EXAMPLES, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}, # ← cached prefix ], messages=[{"role": "user", "content": variable_query}], ) usage = response.usage print(f"cache write: {usage.cache_creation_input_tokens}") print(f"cache read: {usage.cache_read_input_tokens}") print(f"uncached: {usage.input_tokens}") ``` ```python def prompt_cache_economics(prefix_tokens: int, variable_tokens: int, output_tokens: int, requests_per_day: int, model="claude-3-5-sonnet", cache_hit_rate=0.92): """Is prompt caching worth it for this workload?""" p = PRICING_INR_PER_1K[model] write_multiplier = 1.25 # Anthropic charges 1.25× to write the cache no_cache = requests_per_day * ( (prefix_tokens + variable_tokens) / 1000 * p["in"] + output_tokens / 1000 * p["out"]) hits = requests_per_day * cache_hit_rate misses = requests_per_day - hits with_cache = ( misses * (prefix_tokens / 1000 * p["in"] * write_multiplier) + hits * (prefix_tokens / 1000 * p["cached_in"]) + requests_per_day * (variable_tokens / 1000 * p["in"] + output_tokens / 1000 * p["out"])) return { "daily_no_cache_inr": round(no_cache, 2), "daily_with_cache_inr": round(with_cache, 2), "monthly_saving_inr": round((no_cache - with_cache) * 30, 2), "saving_pct": round(100 * (1 - with_cache / no_cache), 1), } print(prompt_cache_economics(prefix_tokens=2800, variable_tokens=400, output_tokens=350, requests_per_day=40_000)) ``` **The structural requirement: stable content first, variable content last.** One varying token at position 3 — a timestamp, a request ID, the user's name — invalidates the entire prefix. ```python def build_cacheable_messages(system: str, few_shots: list[dict], retrieved: str, user_query: str, cache_boundary_after_shots=True) -> list[dict]: """Order content so the cacheable prefix is maximal.""" system_blocks = [{"type": "text", "text": system}] if few_shots: shots_text = "\n\n".join( f"User: {s['user']}\nAssistant: {s['assistant']}" for s in few_shots) system_blocks.append({"type": "text", "text": shots_text}) # Mark the LAST stable block as the cache boundary if cache_boundary_after_shots: system_blocks[-1]["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"} return { "system": system_blocks, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": f"Context:\n{retrieved}\n\nQuestion: {user_query}"}], } ``` **Verify hits in production**, do not assume: ```python CACHE_HITS = Counter("llm_prompt_cache_tokens_total", "Prompt cache tokens", ["feature", "kind"]) def record_cache_usage(feature: str, usage) -> None: CACHE_HITS.labels(feature=feature, kind="read").inc( getattr(usage, "cache_read_input_tokens", 0)) CACHE_HITS.labels(feature=feature, kind="write").inc( getattr(usage, "cache_creation_input_tokens", 0)) CACHE_HITS.labels(feature=feature, kind="uncached").inc(usage.input_tokens) ``` A cache read ratio below about 0.8 on a workload with a long fixed prefix means something in your prefix is varying — go find it. ##### Exact and semantic caching ```python import hashlib import json import numpy as np from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import Optional @dataclass class CacheConfig: prompt_version: str exact_ttl_s: int = 86400 semantic_ttl_s: int = 3600 semantic_threshold: float = 0.97 # ← high. Lower is dangerous. semantic_enabled_features: set = None class TieredCache: def __init__(self, redis_client, vectorstore, embedder, config: CacheConfig): self.redis = redis_client self.vs = vectorstore self.embedder = embedder self.cfg = config def _exact_key(self, messages, model, temperature) -> str: payload = json.dumps( {"m": messages, "model": model, "t": temperature, "v": self.cfg.prompt_version}, sort_keys=True) return "llm:x:" + hashlib.sha256(payload.encode()).hexdigest()[:32] async def get(self, messages, model, temperature, feature: str) -> Optional[dict]: if temperature > 0: return None # never cache sampled output raw = await self.redis.get(self._exact_key(messages, model, temperature)) if raw: return {"response": json.loads(raw), "hit": "exact"} allowed = (self.cfg.semantic_enabled_features is None or feature in self.cfg.semantic_enabled_features) if not allowed: return None query = messages[-1]["content"] vec = self.embedder.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True)[0] res = self.vs.query( query_embeddings=[vec.tolist()], n_results=1, where={"version": self.cfg.prompt_version, "model": model}, include=["metadatas", "distances"]) if res["distances"][0]: similarity = 1 - res["distances"][0][0] if similarity >= self.cfg.semantic_threshold: return {"response": json.loads(res["metadatas"][0][0]["response"]), "hit": "semantic", "similarity": round(similarity, 4)} return None async def put(self, messages, model, temperature, response: dict, feature: str): if temperature > 0: return await self.redis.setex( self._exact_key(messages, model, temperature), self.cfg.exact_ttl_s, json.dumps(response)) allowed = (self.cfg.semantic_enabled_features is None or feature in self.cfg.semantic_enabled_features) if allowed: query = messages[-1]["content"] vec = self.embedder.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True)[0] self.vs.upsert( ids=[hashlib.sha256(query.encode()).hexdigest()[:20]], embeddings=[vec.tolist()], metadatas=[{"response": json.dumps(response), "version": self.cfg.prompt_version, "model": model, "feature": feature}]) ``` **Three safety properties in that code, all learned the hard way:** **Prompt version in the key.** Change the prompt without bumping it and you serve old-prompt responses indefinitely. **Semantic threshold at 0.97.** At 0.85, "what is the Pune delivery SLA" and "what is the Chennai delivery SLA" collide and you serve a confidently wrong cached answer. **The threshold is a correctness parameter, not a tuning knob.** **Per-feature semantic enablement.** Semantic caching is safe for FAQ-style lookup and dangerous for anything where small wording differences change the answer — legal, financial, or personalised responses. ```python def validate_semantic_threshold(cache, test_pairs, embedder): """Find the threshold where distinct questions stop colliding.""" import numpy as np results = [] for threshold in [0.90, 0.93, 0.95, 0.97, 0.99]: false_hits = 0 for q1, q2, should_match in test_pairs: e1 = embedder.encode([q1], normalize_embeddings=True)[0] e2 = embedder.encode([q2], normalize_embeddings=True)[0] sim = float(e1 @ e2) matched = sim >= threshold if matched and not should_match: false_hits += 1 results.append({"threshold": threshold, "false_hits": false_hits, "of": len(test_pairs)}) return results TEST_PAIRS = [ ("What is the Pune delivery SLA?", "What is the Chennai delivery SLA?", False), ("What's the notice period?", "What is the notice period?", True), ("How do I cancel order 4471?", "How do I cancel order 8821?", False), ("Explain the refund policy", "Tell me about refunds", True), ] ``` **Run that validation on your own domain.** The right threshold depends on how much your queries differ by a single entity, and 0.97 is a starting point rather than a universal answer. ##### Model routing and cascades The largest lever, and Day 34 covered the serving side. Here is the cost analysis. ```python from typing import Literal, Callable from pydantic import BaseModel class TierDecision(BaseModel): tier: Literal["nano", "small", "large"] confidence: Literal["high", "medium", "low"] reasoning: str TIERS = { "nano": {"model": "gpt-4o-mini", "inr_1k_out": 0.050}, "small": {"model": "llama-3-8b-selfhost", "inr_1k_out": 0.002}, "large": {"model": "gpt-4o", "inr_1k_out": 0.840}, } class CostAwareRouter: def __init__(self, classifier_model="gpt-4o-mini", escalate_low_confidence=True): self.classifier_model = classifier_model self.escalate = escalate_low_confidence def heuristic_route(self, request: dict) -> Optional[str]: """Free rules first — most requests never need a classifier call.""" task = request.get("task") n_in = request["prompt_tokens"] if task in ("classify", "extract", "route") and n_in < 1500: return "small" if n_in > 8000: return "large" if task == "summarize" and n_in < 4000: return "nano" return None async def route(self, request: dict) -> str: cheap = self.heuristic_route(request) if cheap: return cheap decision = await self._classify(request["prompt"]) if decision.confidence == "low" and self.escalate: return "large" return decision.tier ``` **Heuristics before the classifier.** A classifier call costs ₹0.002 and 200ms; routing 60–70% of traffic on free rules avoids that entirely. **Cascading is better than classification when verification is cheap:** ```python async def verified_cascade(request, verifier, tiers=("small", "large")): """Try cheap, verify, escalate only on failure.""" for i, tier in enumerate(tiers): result = await call_tier(tier, request) if i == len(tiers) - 1: return {**result, "tier": tier, "escalations": i} verdict = await verifier(request, result) if verdict["acceptable"]: return {**result, "tier": tier, "escalations": i} return result def cascade_economics(tier_costs: dict, verify_cost: float, escalation_rate: float): """When does cascading beat always using the large model?""" small, large = tier_costs["small"], tier_costs["large"] cascade = small + verify_cost + escalation_rate * (large + verify_cost) return { "cascade_inr": round(cascade, 4), "always_large_inr": round(large, 4), "saving_pct": round(100 * (1 - cascade / large), 1), "breakeven_escalation_rate": round( (large - small - verify_cost) / (large + verify_cost), 3), "worth_it": cascade < large, } print(cascade_economics({"small": 0.004, "large": 0.180}, verify_cost=0.002, escalation_rate=0.22)) # saving 75.4%, breakeven at escalation rate 0.98 ``` **The break-even escalation rate is usually very high**, which means cascading wins unless your cheap tier fails almost always. That is a strong argument for trying it. **Free verification is the ideal case** — JSON that parses, code that runs, a schema that validates. Day 18's constrained output composes perfectly with cascading, because validity is checkable at zero cost. ##### Context and token reduction Often the lever that improves quality while reducing cost. ```python def context_cost_quality_sweep(eval_set, rag_system, k_values=(3, 5, 8, 12, 20)): """More chunks costs more and frequently scores worse.""" import numpy as np rows = [] for k in k_values: scores, costs, latencies = [], [], [] for case in eval_set: result = rag_system.answer(case["question"], top_k=k) scores.append(judge(case, result["answer"])) costs.append(result["cost_inr"]) latencies.append(result["latency_s"]) rows.append({ "top_k": k, "quality": round(float(np.mean(scores)), 3), "inr_per_query": round(float(np.mean(costs)), 4), "p95_latency_s": round(float(np.percentile(latencies, 95)), 2), "quality_per_rupee": round(float(np.mean(scores)) / max(float(np.mean(costs)), 1e-6), 1), }) return rows ``` A representative result: | top_k | quality | ₹/query | p95 latency | quality/₹ | |---|---|---|---|---| | 3 | 7.9 | 0.021 | 1.8s | 376 | | **5** | **8.4** | **0.031** | 2.1s | **271** | | 8 | 8.3 | 0.046 | 2.6s | 180 | | 12 | 8.1 | 0.064 | 3.2s | 127 | | 20 | 7.6 | 0.098 | 4.4s | 78 | **Quality peaks at 5 and declines after.** This is the "lost in the middle" effect from Day 36, and it means the Pune team's `top_k=15` was paying 2× for measurably worse answers. **Other token reductions:** ```python def audit_system_prompt(prompt: str, tokenizer) -> dict: """Most system prompts are 20-40% padding.""" lines = [l for l in prompt.split("\n") if l.strip()] tokens = len(tokenizer.encode(prompt)) filler_markers = ["please note", "it is important", "remember that", "you should always", "make sure to", "as an ai"] filler_lines = [l for l in lines if any(m in l.lower() for m in filler_markers)] return { "total_tokens": tokens, "lines": len(lines), "likely_filler_lines": len(filler_lines), "examples": filler_lines[:5], "estimated_reducible_pct": round(100 * len(filler_lines) / len(lines), 1), } ``` **Cap `max_tokens` per feature.** Output tokens cost 3–5× input tokens, and a classification task producing 500 tokens when 20 would do is pure waste: ```python MAX_TOKENS_BY_TASK = { "classify": 32, "extract": 512, "summarize": 300, "answer": 400, "explain": 800, "draft": 1200, } ``` ##### Batch processing Half price for work that can wait. ```python import json from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI() def submit_batch(requests: list[dict], model="gpt-4o-mini", output_path="batch_input.jsonl") -> str: """50% discount, 24h SLA. For anything not user-facing.""" with open(output_path, "w") as f: for i, req in enumerate(requests): f.write(json.dumps({ "custom_id": req.get("id", f"req-{i}"), "method": "POST", "url": "/v1/chat/completions", "body": {"model": model, "messages": req["messages"], "max_tokens": req.get("max_tokens", 512), "temperature": 0.0}, }) + "\n") uploaded = client.files.create(file=open(output_path, "rb"), purpose="batch") batch = client.batches.create( input_file_id=uploaded.id, endpoint="/v1/chat/completions", completion_window="24h") return batch.id ``` **Candidates for batch processing:** nightly document ingestion and enrichment, evaluation suite runs, synthetic data generation, backfilling embeddings, and periodic re-summarisation. In most products this is 30–50% of total LLM volume and it is all eligible. ##### Self-hosting break-even ```python @dataclass class SelfHostAnalysis: api_inr_per_m_tokens: float gpu_hourly_inr: float throughput_tok_s: float utilisation: float = 0.50 engineering_monthly_inr: float = 180_000 replicas: int = 2 def analyse(self, monthly_tokens_m: float) -> dict: api_cost = monthly_tokens_m * self.api_inr_per_m_tokens gpu_monthly = self.gpu_hourly_inr * 24 * 30 * self.replicas capacity_m = (self.throughput_tok_s * 3600 * 24 * 30 * self.utilisation * self.replicas / 1e6) self_host = gpu_monthly + self.engineering_monthly_inr breakeven_m = self_host / self.api_inr_per_m_tokens return { "monthly_tokens_m": monthly_tokens_m, "api_cost_inr": round(api_cost), "self_host_cost_inr": round(self_host), "capacity_m_tokens": round(capacity_m), "breakeven_m_tokens": round(breakeven_m), "sufficient_capacity": monthly_tokens_m <= capacity_m, "recommendation": ( "self-host" if monthly_tokens_m > breakeven_m and monthly_tokens_m <= capacity_m else "use API"), } analysis = SelfHostAnalysis(api_inr_per_m_tokens=210, gpu_hourly_inr=250, throughput_tok_s=5900) for volume in [50, 200, 800, 3000]: print(analysis.analyse(volume)) ``` **Include engineering cost.** A self-hosted stack needs someone to run it — upgrades, incidents, capacity planning — and omitting that is how teams conclude self-hosting saves money when it does not. **The hybrid pattern is usually right:** self-host the high-volume simple tier, use APIs for the low-volume complex tier. You get the cost benefit where volume justifies it and avoid operating a 70B deployment for 5% of traffic. ##### Assembling the optimised layer ```python class CostOptimizedInference: """Cache → route → cascade → generate, with attribution throughout.""" def __init__(self, cache: TieredCache, router: CostAwareRouter, tiers: dict, verifier=None, budget=None): self.cache, self.router = cache, router self.tiers, self.verifier, self.budget = tiers, verifier, budget async def complete(self, request: dict) -> dict: feature = request["feature"] t0 = time.perf_counter() if self.budget: self.budget.check(feature) cached = await self.cache.get( request["messages"], request.get("model", "auto"), request.get("temperature", 0.0), feature) if cached: return {**cached["response"], "cost_inr": 0.0, "cache_status": cached["hit"], "latency_ms": round((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000, 1)} tier = await self.router.route(request) messages = build_cacheable_messages(**request["prompt_parts"]) if self.verifier and tier != "large": result = await verified_cascade( {**request, "messages": messages}, self.verifier, tiers=(tier, "large")) else: result = await call_tier(tier, {**request, "messages": messages}) await self.cache.put(request["messages"], result["model"], request.get("temperature", 0.0), result, feature) if self.budget: self.budget.record(feature, result["cost_inr"]) return {**result, "cache_status": "miss", "latency_ms": round((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000, 1)} ``` **Order matters.** Cache before routing — a hit costs nothing regardless of which tier would have served it. Route before generating. Verify before escalating. ##### Budget enforcement ```python class BudgetGuard: """Enforce spend limits in code, not just in the dashboard.""" def __init__(self, redis_client, limits_inr: dict, alert_at=0.8): self.redis = redis_client self.limits = limits_inr # {"feature": daily_limit_inr} self.alert_at = alert_at def _key(self, feature: str) -> str: from datetime import datetime return f"spend:{feature}:{datetime.utcnow():%Y-%m-%d}" async def check(self, feature: str) -> None: limit = self.limits.get(feature) if limit is None: return spent = float(await self.redis.get(self._key(feature)) or 0) if spent >= limit: raise BudgetExceeded( f"{feature} reached its daily cap of ₹{limit:,.0f}") if spent >= limit * self.alert_at: logger.warning("budget_warning feature=%s spent=%.0f limit=%.0f", feature, spent, limit) async def record(self, feature: str, cost_inr: float) -> None: key = self._key(feature) await self.redis.incrbyfloat(key, cost_inr) await self.redis.expire(key, 172_800) ``` **A dashboard alert arrives after the spend.** A code-level cap prevents it — and it is the difference between a ₹40,000 surprise and a feature degrading gracefully. ##### The optimisation plan The assignment. Prioritise by saving per unit of effort. ```python @dataclass class OptimizationOpportunity: lever: str estimated_monthly_saving_inr: float effort_days: float quality_risk: Literal["none", "low", "medium", "high"] dependencies: list[str] = field(default_factory=list) @property def roi(self) -> float: return self.estimated_monthly_saving_inr / max(self.effort_days, 0.5) def build_optimization_plan(waste: dict, monthly_spend: float, ) -> list[OptimizationOpportunity]: opportunities = [] if waste["uncached_prefix_pct"] > 5: opportunities.append(OptimizationOpportunity( "Enable prompt caching on the fixed prefix", monthly_spend * waste["uncached_prefix_pct"] / 100 * 0.85, effort_days=0.5, quality_risk="none")) if waste["duplicate_waste_pct"] > 5: opportunities.append(OptimizationOpportunity( "Exact-match response cache", monthly_spend * waste["duplicate_waste_pct"] / 100 * 0.95, effort_days=2, quality_risk="none")) if waste["model_overkill_pct"] > 10: opportunities.append(OptimizationOpportunity( "Model routing with verified cascade", monthly_spend * waste["model_overkill_pct"] / 100 * 0.70, effort_days=5, quality_risk="low", dependencies=["evaluation suite"])) if waste["output_heavy_pct"] > 10: opportunities.append(OptimizationOpportunity( "Per-task max_tokens caps and brevity prompting", monthly_spend * waste["output_heavy_pct"] / 100 * 0.30, effort_days=1, quality_risk="low")) return sorted(opportunities, key=lambda o: -o.roi) ``` The Pune plan, produced by exactly this analysis: | Lever | Monthly saving | Effort | Risk | ROI | |---|---|---|---|---| | Prompt caching | ₹1.41 L | 0.5 d | none | 2.82 L/d | | `max_tokens` caps | ₹0.55 L | 1 d | low | 0.55 L/d | | Exact cache | ₹3.15 L | 2 d | none | 1.58 L/d | | Reduce `top_k` 15→5 | ₹2.21 L | 1 d | **improved** | 2.21 L/d | | Model routing | ₹5.67 L | 5 d | low | 1.13 L/d | **Total: ₹12.99 lakh a month for 9.5 days of work.** Ordering by ROI means the first 1.5 days delivered ₹1.96 lakh, which is what gets the remaining work approved. ##### Common mistakes - **Optimising before instrumenting** — you will pick the wrong lever. - **One API key across features**, making attribution impossible. - **Semantic cache threshold below 0.95** — a correctness bug, not a tuning choice. - **No prompt version in the cache key.** - **Variable content at the start of the prompt**, destroying prefix cache hits. - **Assuming more retrieved chunks means better answers** — it usually means worse and costlier. - **No `max_tokens` cap**, letting a classification task generate 500 tokens. - **Skipping batch API** for work that is not user-facing. - **Ignoring engineering cost** in the self-hosting break-even. - **No code-level budget cap**, so the dashboard alert arrives after the spend. - **Caching sampled output** at temperature above zero. - **Assuming cost reduction means quality reduction.** It usually means removing waste. ##### Hands-on: measure the waste first Your practical task adds semantic and prompt caching and measures the cost reduction on realistic traffic. **Run `waste_analysis` before implementing anything** — if your duplicate rate is 3%, a semantic cache is not your lever and you will have spent two days for nothing. Validate your semantic threshold against the collision test pairs on your own domain before enabling it. The mini project builds a cost-optimised inference layer with a cascade and caching, reporting cost per query before and after. Include the quality measurement in both configurations; a 70% cost reduction that loses four points of accuracy is a different result from one that loses nothing, and only the second is a win. Log `cache_status` and `tier` on every request so you can see the distribution. The assignment audits a product's cost structure and proposes a prioritised plan. Use the ROI ordering — saving divided by effort days — and state the quality risk for each lever explicitly. Lead with the two zero-risk levers, because getting those shipped in the first week is what buys credibility for the larger changes. ##### Key takeaways - **Instrument before optimising.** Attribute cost by feature, model, and request type; the largest waste category is rarely the one you expected. - **Prompt caching is the highest return per unit of effort** — often a single argument — and it requires stable content first, variable content last. - **Semantic cache thresholds below 0.95 are a correctness bug**, not a tuning choice; validate against collision pairs from your own domain. - **Model routing and cascading are the largest lever**, and the break-even escalation rate is usually so high that cascading wins. - **Reducing retrieved chunks often improves quality while cutting cost** — cost optimisation in GenAI is mostly about removing waste, not accepting worse output.
